name: Chicago Drill
summary: Visually and culturally, it established a gritty, unfiltered "documentary" style of music video and a distinct fashion aesthetic centered on designer denim and streetwear (particularly True Religion).
description:
Visually and culturally, it established a gritty, unfiltered "documentary" style of music video and a distinct fashion aesthetic centered on designer denim and streetwear (particularly True Religion).

While the genre was initially defined by its hyper-local focus on Chicago gang culture, it rapidly expanded into a global phenomenon, influencing the development of UK Drill in London and Brooklyn Drill in New York.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Authenticity, nihilism, loyalty, survival, unfiltered reality ("Chiraq")

fashion.Overview: Fashion was a central component of the early Drill scene, heavily influenced by Chief Keef's personal style. In 2012, Keef proclaimed himself a "True Religion Fein" (fiend), cementing the denim brand True Religion as the uniform of the movement. The standard look involved baggy True Religion jeans, jean jackets, baseball shirts, and V-neck t-shirts. This aesthetic was so influential that a decade later, Chief Keef officially collaborated with the brand to design a collection featuring flames, cartoon skulls, and bubble letters, solidifying the look's legacy.
